scenarios.title: Local save while the provider is unavailable
scenarios.summary: With a healthy, unlocked private store, edits appear immediately. One local database transaction saves their exact history and required records before acknowledgment. Copying that history to the provider can wait.
scenarios.setup: A returning Mac has a healthy, unlocked, exclusively owned private store. The user edits “Packing” while the provider is unavailable.
scenarios.outcome: After the complete local commit, the edit survives reopening and remains queued for exact publication.

steps.title: Edit admission and pending-generation registration
steps.user: The text and synchronous search results update immediately. The edit is pending.
steps.operation: Admit the edit into the live model and record its generation, before-state and action context.
steps.rule: Local health, key and lifecycle gates govern admission; provider waiting alone does not block it.

steps.title: Capture, sealing and atomic local acceptance
steps.user: Typing continues while the captured generation is encoded off the main thread.
steps.operation: Freeze the complete action, seal once, then atomically commit exact bytes, acceptance/indexes, retained pin and wakeups.
steps.rule: A qualified complete SQL commit is the local durability barrier. Capture scheduling is not an acknowledgment.

steps.title: Reopening from local history before publication
steps.user: Packing contains the durable edit and is searchable. Sync remains pending.
steps.operation: Recover the accepted suffix, load complete current rows/context, and later publish the same retained sealed objects.
steps.rule: Upload and plaintext installation are separate outcomes; local durability does not depend on either.

scenarios.title: Crash recovery before and after the local commit
scenarios.summary: An edit is recoverable after its complete local transaction commits, even if the acknowledgment was lost. Text still held only in memory remains within the pending loss window.
scenarios.setup: “Trip” has a durable value A and a pending value B. Power is lost at different points in the next save.
scenarios.outcome: Recovery includes complete committed groups, including a commit whose callback was lost. RAM-only edits retain an explicit loss window.

steps.title: Pending value B before the durability barrier
steps.user: B is visible with pending work; it has no completed durability acknowledgment.
steps.operation: Capture/sealing may be scheduled, but the previous accepted closure A remains the recovery baseline.
steps.rule: The existing 2.7-second idle and 15-second first-pending timers are scheduling targets, not per-keystroke durability promises.

steps.title: Interruption of the acceptance transaction
steps.user: Before a qualified commit, B is unacknowledged. After a complete commit, its durable identity exists even without a callback.
steps.operation: SQLite resolves transaction state; exact object bytes and complete action/index/pin/wakeup bookkeeping succeed together.
steps.rule: There is no accepted partial action and no second NV note-value WAL.

steps.title: Recovery from complete committed evidence
steps.user: The recovered model shows A or committed B according to the durable evidence.
steps.operation: Query exact committed identities, drain required work and materialize the complete history through the accepted local commit before editable publication.
steps.rule: Neither an upload flag nor a lost UI completion determines whether the action committed.

scenarios.title: Delayed save completion with a newer pending generation
scenarios.summary: Save E captures AB. The user then types C, creating newer edit F with ABC. Completion of E clears only E’s pending work; F stays pending and the displayed text stays ABC.
scenarios.setup: Capture E contains “AB”. While E saves, another keystroke produces newer generation F with “ABC”.
scenarios.outcome: E may settle its own generation; F remains pending until its own complete barrier succeeds.

steps.title: Frozen capture E containing AB
steps.user: The sealer works on AB while the editor remains responsive.
steps.operation: Copy complete E values/action metadata and bind the capture to exact pending generations.
steps.rule: One collection sealer owns immutable retry input; later edits cannot alter that capture.

steps.title: Admission of F containing ABC while E is in flight
steps.user: The live note is ABC; F is a distinct newer pending generation.
steps.operation: Preserve F and its dependent causal context while E finishes its own SQL acceptance.
steps.rule: A captured value is not a snapshot of all work that will exist at completion time.

steps.title: Settlement of E without clearing F
steps.user: ABC stays visible and pending. E cannot clear F or write AB over it.
steps.operation: Settle only serviced generations; separately validate any prepared model publication and capture F next.
steps.rule: Durable record completion and generation-fenced live publication have separate applicability checks.

scenarios.title: Returning startup with optional snapshot work queued
scenarios.summary: Startup finishes required receive work and unfinished checks, then reads all current notes and editing context together. Independent optional snapshots continue after the complete editable model is published.
scenarios.setup: The returning store has valid current rows plus a small accepted suffix, a large old history, and an independent optional snapshot waiting.
scenarios.outcome: All current notes and authoring context publish together; optional history preparation continues after that checked handoff.

steps.title: Recovery of startup-required work
steps.user: Opening waits for known required Changes and prerequisites, not arbitrary queue order.
steps.operation: Drain durable required work and unfinished verification; leave independent optional snapshot assembly durably queued.
steps.rule: Bootstrap, known damage and required dependencies still gate success.

steps.title: Consistent capture and publication of complete current state
steps.user: Every current body and synchronous-search index is ready before editing begins.
steps.operation: Decode complete current rows and compact authoring frontiers directly into final unpublished memory under one consistent read capture.
steps.rule: Check scope, decoding formats, view version and accepted/current-row history positions; final owner checks prevent stale publication.

steps.title: Optional intake after successful host publication
steps.user: The complete current model accepts input and serves synchronous search while optional history/snapshot work proceeds in bounded background turns.
steps.operation: Reserve the receive owner after successful publication; resume optional validation and lazy scoped history queries.
steps.rule: Finite saves settling must allow progress without another delivery. Required persistence takes priority over optional maintenance.

scenarios.title: Startup with positively disclosed but unreadable newer evidence
scenarios.summary: Work Offline can open complete local history when startup is waiting for a particular, positively disclosed newer object. Ordinary provider unavailability is a synchronization status and needs no such choice.
scenarios.setup: Local history is complete. At startup the provider positively discloses newer required object R, whose bytes cannot yet be read.
scenarios.outcome: Work Offline opens the complete local closure and preserves the obligation to reconcile R later.

steps.title: Positive disclosure of named unread evidence R
steps.user: Startup shows a bounded wait for R and offers Work Offline or Save Current Collection As….
steps.operation: Record positive disclosure and distinguish it from generic offline, quota, permission or timeout status.
steps.rule: An evicted provider copy already retained exactly in the private store creates no such wait.

steps.title: Explicit continuation from the complete local closure
steps.user: All locally durable notes remain editable and searchable.
steps.operation: Publish the healthy local closure after ordinary ownership/key/startup gates; fence affected provider effects.
steps.rule: This choice does not declare R absent, resolved or safe to overwrite. Generic provider unavailability needs no Work Offline prompt.

steps.title: Reconciliation when R becomes readable
steps.user: New history reconciles with any local edits without revoking the active session’s editability.
steps.operation: Retain and validate R, resolve dependencies, then prepare and generation-check its reduction.
steps.rule: Late positive disclosure in an already editing session is pending sync status, not a retroactive startup gate.

scenarios.title: Reconstruction of invalid derived current rows
scenarios.summary: Invalid current-note rows, decoding dictionaries or history-position bindings require rebuilding from healthy retained history. The new view installs together while required private records and pending work stay preserved.
scenarios.setup: Retained history is healthy, but a current-cell codec/dictionary or represented-prefix binding is invalid.
scenarios.outcome: Reconstruct the complete current model from validated history, preserving settings, association and pending work.

steps.title: Classification of derived-row invalidity
steps.user: Opening reports reconstruction instead of showing an empty or partial collection.
steps.operation: Separate current-row/dictionary/view invalidity from retained-history or required-private-state damage.
steps.rule: A damaged required pin, association or shared database takes the repair path; it cannot be treated as a disposable row.

steps.title: Rebuild through the captured local history position
steps.user: Recovery prepares every note and compact authoring context off the main thread.
steps.operation: Verify the snapshot’s represented history, include every other accepted action, and compute complete final values and editing context.
steps.rule: Snapshot values alone cannot omit earlier branches, Deletes, restorations or compensation context.

steps.title: Generation-checked installation of the complete derived view
steps.user: The complete collection reopens with its settings and pending decisions intact.
steps.operation: Atomically install complete rows/context with a fresh epoch only while owner, accepted target and starting view still match.
steps.rule: Required private groups and history remain independently durable; interference forces recapture.

scenarios.title: Restart during retained-history verification
scenarios.summary: Save a verification request before checking accepted history that might be damaged. If checking or recording its result is interrupted, reopening repeats that exact obligation before publishing an editable model.
scenarios.setup: An on-demand history read may discover damage. The process can crash or fail a diagnosis write before recording its result.
scenarios.outcome: A durable verification obligation is replayed before editing; it rechecks evidence instead of replaying a user command.

steps.title: Durable registration of the verification scope
steps.user: The operation enters verification with an exact, recoverable scope.
steps.operation: Durably retain a host-private request before checking accepted evidence whose damage diagnosis could otherwise disappear.
steps.rule: A successful normal open with no unfinished requests keeps the indexed startup path.

steps.title: Interrupted verification, diagnosis or settlement
steps.user: The app retains the unfinished request, even if writing a damage marker fails.
steps.operation: Check exact bytes through graph/reducer validation; fence the live owner immediately on discovered damage.
steps.rule: Only completed verification settles that request; storage failure leaves a replayable obligation.

steps.title: Replay of the unfinished verification request
steps.user: Editing waits for the required check or an explicit repair/recovery outcome.
steps.operation: Replay the retained scope, then atomically settle it or replace it with the diagnosed damage marker.
steps.rule: Cancellation/close never turn an unfinished check into a successful one; retries are bounded.

scenarios.title: Receipt of a Delete before its parent edit
scenarios.summary: Mac B receives Delete D before the edit P that D observes. It saves D and the missing-input wait across restart. When P arrives, B validates and accepts the complete required history before applying the result.
scenarios.setup: Mac A creates edit P then Delete D observing P. Mac B receives D first and restarts before P arrives.
scenarios.outcome: B retains D as waiting evidence and applies the complete validated closure only after P is durable locally.

steps.title: Retention of D while parent P is missing
steps.user: Mac B keeps its current note; the incomplete child is not yet an applied Delete.
steps.operation: Retain exact D bytes, record named dependencies and atomically park reverse waits.
steps.rule: Stored bytes, accepted causal history and live publication are separate states.

steps.title: Receipt of P and validation of D’s complete closure
steps.user: The durable waiting obligation survives the restart.
steps.operation: Retain/validate P, wake affected dependents and validate D’s entire action/parent closure.
steps.rule: A rejected prerequisite blocks its dependents without discarding shared evidence or accepting a valid-looking prefix.

steps.title: Publication of the accepted causal result
steps.user: B now reflects the applicable Delete without emitting a new local echo action.
steps.operation: Reduce the accepted operation set and publish atomically after current generation checks.
steps.rule: Incoming Delete affects a logical birth; it never grants permission to unlink a remembered filename.

scenarios.title: Publication retry after an uncertain completion
scenarios.summary: Retry uses the same saved bytes and identity. An equal existing file still needs verification and directory durability steps. Conflicting occupants are preserved; receiving an object twice creates one logical action.
scenarios.setup: A locally durable segment was installed at the provider, but its completion was lost. A duplicate or conflicting final name appears.
scenarios.outcome: Retry the same sealed bytes and identity; verify final/directory barriers and preserve conflicting evidence.

steps.title: Selection of exact locally accepted publication input
steps.user: Pending sync selects objects already protected by the local barrier.
steps.operation: Capture the accepted local history position and retrieve its exact sealed objects and descriptors for publication.
steps.rule: A publication retry never reseals changed values under an old operation identity or nonce.

steps.title: Verification of final names and installation barriers
steps.user: An equal final can complete a verified retry. A foreign/wrong-kind/contradictory occupant is preserved.
steps.operation: Use held rooted parents, exclusive creation, exact final-byte checks and required namespace barriers; clean only owned disposable stages.
steps.rule: Equal bytes alone do not prove provider installation durability or physical ownership.

steps.title: Idempotent receipt of duplicate objects
steps.user: Mac B adds one semantic action, even if filenames or notifications differ.
steps.operation: Validate bounded bytes and complete identity, deduplicate accepted set insertion, and retain independent legitimate branches.
steps.rule: Listings and callbacks are discovery opportunities; omissions, sequence holes and empty passes do not certify completeness.

scenarios.title: Automatic merge of strictly separated line edits
scenarios.summary: Two revisions share one unambiguous base. One changes line 1 and the other line 3, leaving an unchanged line between them. If all fields satisfy the conservative rules, the combined Current retains both inputs.
scenarios.setup: Both Macs know “Bread / Milk / Apples” on three LF-separated lines. A changes line 1 to Sourdough; B changes line 3 to Pears.
scenarios.outcome: With exactly two eligible heads and a unique common base, Current becomes “Sourdough / Milk / Pears”; both inputs remain history.

steps.title: Independent revisions from one common base
steps.user: A sees its first-line edit; B sees its last-line edit.
steps.operation: Capture distinct complete actions with the exact represented note predecessors and scope parents.
steps.rule: Dates and arrival order supply no winner; exact stored UTF-8/CRLF/LF distinctions are preserved.

steps.title: Validation of heads, base and separated edit intervals
steps.user: Each receiver retains both complete branches before attempting a merge.
steps.operation: Derive exact note heads and the unique best common base; calculate one prefix/suffix-bounded edit per branch.
steps.rule: Only strictly separated intervals merge. Other fields must also satisfy their rules, together as one result.

steps.title: Fenced publication of the derived combined Current
steps.user: The three lines read Sourdough, Milk, Pears. Both branch IDs remain inspectable.
steps.operation: Publish the complete derived value and its represented inputs after a live-generation recheck.
steps.rule: Automatic recomputation does not mint a random local merge action; third-head or stale inputs require recomputation/review.

scenarios.title: Review after overlapping edits or a third head
scenarios.summary: Touching or overlapping edits, an ambiguous base, a third revision or the two-sided line limit require review. Every alternative stays available. A prepared choice must still match the complete current inputs when admitted.
scenarios.setup: Two Macs replace “Milk” differently, or a third independent head arrives while a two-head merge is being prepared.
scenarios.outcome: Preserve all alternatives and offer review instead of electing a timestamp winner or pairwise folding three branches.

steps.title: Discovery of incompatible exact heads
steps.user: Current has unresolved alternatives, even if two previews happen to look equal.
steps.operation: Retain exact revisions and build deterministic head/represented-input evidence.
steps.rule: Touching edit intervals, same-boundary insertions, ambiguous best bases, and two-sided bodies over 10,000 lines require review.

steps.title: Invalidation of a two-head preparation by a third head
steps.user: A prepared two-input result cannot overwrite the now-current three-head state.
steps.operation: Recheck the complete head set, generation and represented inputs immediately before publication or choice admission.
steps.rule: Three heads are not pairwise merged into an invented winner; equal values do not erase revision identities.

steps.title: Preparation and admission of an explicit applicable choice
steps.user: The resolver previews exact alternatives. Dismissal before admission leaves note state and history unchanged.
steps.operation: An explicit applicable choice captures its exact scope, then takes the ordinary complete local action barrier.
steps.rule: Preview is side-effect free; changed inputs require new preparation and consent.

scenarios.title: Ordinary editing of one unresolved head
scenarios.summary: Editing displayed revision A replaces the represented A input. Known conflicting revision B stays unresolved. Releasing the temporary editing pin schedules computation from the full set of applicable note heads.
scenarios.setup: Current represents A while incompatible head B is known. The user edits A to A′ before explicitly resolving B.
scenarios.outcome: The ordinary edit supersedes its represented A input and preserves B and independently edited conflict notes.

steps.title: Current A with unresolved alternative B
steps.user: The editor shows A; conflict attention retains B.
steps.operation: Pair Current with its actual represented note inputs and keep the full applied causal action frontier.
steps.rule: Action awareness and note supersession answer different questions.

steps.title: Ordinary edit from represented A to A′
steps.user: A′ is visible and pending; B is still an alternative.
steps.operation: Freeze a faithful action before/after pair and predecessor set for Current’s represented A, without silently widening it to B.
steps.rule: An explicit resolution or valid automatic merge needs its own complete represented-input evidence.

steps.title: Reduction after release of the temporary Current-head pin
steps.user: After the exact local barrier, the full applied head set is reduced again.
steps.operation: Schedule reduction/publication when the temporary editing pin is released, even without another provider callback.
steps.rule: Keep independently edited conflict copies; generation checks protect newer typing.

scenarios.title: Concurrent Delete and offline edit on separate Macs
scenarios.summary: Delete D and edit E are created independently from the same note. History reduction deletes the old note birth and preserves eligible concurrent E in a deterministic conflict note. An edit already observed by D is covered instead.
scenarios.setup: A and B know the same note. A deletes it while B independently edits it without observing the Delete.
scenarios.outcome: The old birth is deleted, while an otherwise eligible concurrent edit is preserved in a deterministic conflict birth.

steps.title: Independent local acceptance of Delete and edit
steps.user: Each Mac completes its own full local action/parent barrier.
steps.operation: Record the Delete’s causal inputs and B’s separate note revision exactly.
steps.rule: Logical deletion requires applicable explicit history; a missing provider file is not that intent.

steps.title: Reduction of the complete Delete/edit history
steps.user: The deleted source birth leaves Current; B’s concurrent value remains recoverable.
steps.operation: Reduce causal Delete/edit relationships and derive the eligible deterministic automatic-preservation birth.
steps.rule: An edit already observed by the Delete is covered; an edit descended from the Delete does not revive the old birth.

steps.title: Inspection and fresh-birth restoration of deleted history
steps.user: History/Recently Deleted retains exact prior branches. Explicit restoration creates a fresh birth.
steps.operation: Derive deleted-history entries and restoration provenance separately from filesystem Trash.
steps.rule: An incoming Delete cannot physically remove a remembered path; the original exact-snapshot operation owns any such effect.

scenarios.title: Retraction after a later Delete covers a preserved edit
scenarios.summary: Delete concurrent with E creates automatic conflict note C. A later Delete observing E can remove untouched C when no eligible source remains. Independent edits to C and still-eligible descendants of E survive.
scenarios.setup: D₀ races with E, creating automatic copy C. Later D₁ observes E. In one branch C is untouched; in another C was edited to P.
scenarios.outcome: Retraction removes an ineligible untouched automatic copy; P and any still-eligible independent descendant survive.

steps.title: Derivation of automatic copy C for concurrent E
steps.user: C appears because E is not covered by D₀.
steps.operation: Retain source/provenance evidence for the deterministic automatic result.
steps.rule: Automatic preservation is derived from complete history, not a new independent user import.

steps.title: Reevaluation after D₁ observes E
steps.user: Eligibility is recomputed for the source and its preservation result.
steps.operation: Prepare retraction only if C has no independent edit and no remaining eligible source value.
steps.rule: A new F descended from E but concurrent with D₁ still deserves preservation; P is independent work.

steps.title: Fenced retraction and projection reconciliation
steps.user: Untouched C disappears; independently edited P stays. Uncertain external bytes remain pending.
steps.operation: Generation-fence the model transition and inspect any exact projection before cleanup/import classification.
steps.rule: Do not create blind retirement/unlink effects or echo-import the obsolete automatic projection.

scenarios.title: Snapshot state and required parent objects
scenarios.summary: A general v1 snapshot can name an accepted parent snapshot independently of the history represented by its values. Acceptance updates the required-object frontier together. Parent objects and all accepted operations outside the snapshot’s represented history stay available.
scenarios.setup: General snapshot S₂ names accepted S₁ as a retention parent. A snapshot created later can represent an earlier set of logical operations.
scenarios.outcome: Exact parent closure stays retained; Current and Undo still derive from complete accepted operations, not snapshot age.

steps.title: Capture accepted history and uncovered snapshot roots
steps.user: Snapshot preparation captures a consistent local history position and exact accepted roots not covered by another root.
steps.operation: Prepare bounded pages/root and explicit supported retention-parent locators from checked evidence.
steps.rule: Snapshot retention parents cover object closure; note predecessors and action scope parents have separate roles.

steps.title: Atomic acceptance of S₂ and its exact parent evidence
steps.user: S₁ remains durable while the accepted root frontier advances.
steps.operation: Atomically retain root/pages, accepted membership, parent edges and wakeups; remove only explicitly named parent tips.
steps.rule: Concurrent independent roots remain tips. Empty parent sets use the same eight-category v1 layout. Missing supported dependencies wait normally.

steps.title: Reconstruct with accepted work outside the snapshot
steps.user: Notes, conflicts, deleted history and Undo still include accepted operations outside the snapshot’s represented history.
steps.operation: Reuse checked logical traversal and retained closure, then reconstruct the complete target prefix if needed.
steps.rule: Representing earlier history never rolls Current back or permits removing required ancestor bytes. Snapshot chains can reduce the number of roots checked at startup.

scenarios.title: Historical body restoration with current title and labels
scenarios.summary: Note History can supply an older body for a new recovery action. Current title and labels stay unchanged unless explicitly selected. Admission checks the complete preview and current note again.
scenarios.setup: “Travel 2027” has a current title and labels. The user opens Note History and selects an older body while retaining those current fields.
scenarios.outcome: A newly admitted historical-recovery action restores the selected fields after Current revalidation; the old history remains.

steps.title: Read-only preview of a retained historical body
steps.user: History shows read-only Current, known branches and informational dates. Preview changes nothing.
steps.operation: Load a scoped historical query from retained exact revision/action evidence.
steps.rule: The viewer is not a promise of complete global timeline or full-history search; late results cannot reopen a dismissed view.

steps.title: Selection of body restoration against exact Current
steps.user: The review shows today’s title/labels preserved and the chosen historical body.
steps.operation: Capture the selected fields and complete preview with Current’s exact birth, value and generation.
steps.rule: Body is the default selection; title/labels require explicit selection. Stale Current requires fresh preparation.

steps.title: Acceptance of the new historical-recovery action
steps.user: The restored body is ordinary current work with a durable source link and an actual inverse.
steps.operation: Admit the complete group, then seal/accept it through the ordinary local barrier.
steps.rule: Save as new note is a separate fresh-birth action; history recovery neither disposes conflict heads nor resolves Apple versions.

scenarios.title: Named restoration followed by deletion of the fresh birth
scenarios.summary: Restore creates a new note birth linked to the selected deleted entry. Only complete durable restoration evidence removes that source entry from the default list. Deleting the restored note creates a separate entry.
scenarios.setup: “Ideas” appears in Recently Deleted. The user restores its named entry, then later deletes the restored birth.
scenarios.outcome: The original entry leaves the default list only after durable restoration evidence. The later Delete creates its own entry.

steps.title: Selection of a named deleted-history entry
steps.user: A separate read-only viewer offers Restore and shows prior recoverable branches.
steps.operation: Derive the entry from applicable Delete and exact revision/action evidence.
steps.rule: This is retained note history, independent of Trash and any physical-file sweep.

steps.title: Restore admission and durability for fresh birth R
steps.user: R is pending until its complete local action and source provenance are durable.
steps.operation: Capture a fresh birth with exact restoredFrom deletion/revision evidence and commit it with its action.
steps.rule: Only completed named restoration hides the source entry; generic historical copies do not. Projection/upload need not finish.

steps.title: Later deletion of R or concurrent independent restoration
steps.user: R’s Delete yields a new entry; a concurrent explicit restore on another Mac has its own birth.
steps.operation: Retain the old source restoration link even if R is edited or deleted; reduce each fresh birth independently.
steps.rule: The original entry does not reappear based on whether R is live. Concurrent restores may both remain.

scenarios.title: Causal Undo after relaunch or on another Mac
scenarios.summary: Saved action records retain their members, before/after values and Undo relationships. Any Mac can reverse an eligible action when it is the sole candidate at the end of the relevant Undo relationships. Concurrent or overlapping candidates need review; a bulk action is admitted as a complete group.
scenarios.setup: Mac A renames a note. After the action is durably synced, Mac B opens it and invokes Undo Rename.
scenarios.outcome: A unique applicable maximal action can be compensated on B; the new complete action preserves unrelated current changes.

steps.title: Capture and acceptance of the rename action on Mac A
steps.user: A sees the new title; its saved action includes exact before/after references and scope parents.
steps.operation: Freeze operation members, origin provenance and every maximal action represented by the captured applied frontier.
steps.rule: Received-but-unapplied bytes and incompletely loaded history rows do not define the writer’s scope.

steps.title: Derivation of Mac B’s applicable maximal Undo candidate
steps.user: B offers the unique causally maximal applicable rename, regardless of its origin or arrival time.
steps.operation: Build a scoped candidate view from validated action/scope-parent/compensation evidence and actual Current.
steps.rule: Old NSUndoManager entries, selectors and pointers are not persisted. Incomparable/overlapping candidates require review.

steps.title: Admission and acceptance of complete guarded compensation
steps.user: The title reverses while unrelated body/labels remain. History and causal eligibility recover together.
steps.operation: Admit all compensation members or none, then commit its complete action/parent closure.
steps.rule: Bulk work is wholly revalidated; oversized groups must be disclosed as separate independently undoable batches before admission.

scenarios.title: Reviewed Undo with an actual-current inverse
scenarios.summary: Rename B changed Shopping to Groceries, while a represented concurrent action made Current Errands. Approved Undo B records Errands to Shopping. Redo reverses that actual compensation back to Errands.
scenarios.setup: Rename B was Shopping → Groceries. A represented concurrent action supplies Current = Errands. The user selects B through Undo review and explicitly approves replacement with Shopping.
scenarios.outcome: The new compensation records Errands → Shopping; its Redo returns to Errands, while preserving the remaining eligible redo chain.

steps.title: Undo B preparation against represented Current Errands
steps.user: A dismissible read-only review explains the overlap and the captured candidate frontier.
steps.operation: Prepare the actual proposed compensation from Errands to approved Shopping in the invocation’s Undo mode.
steps.rule: Preview/Cancel consumes nothing. Note History and conflict commands remain distinct even with identical text.

steps.title: Approval and admission of Errands → Shopping
steps.user: Shopping becomes pending only if the captured Current and candidate frontier still match.
steps.operation: Freeze actual before = Errands and after = Shopping, with exact undoOf/action/causal evidence.
steps.rule: Approval does not bypass missing evidence, no-op checks, format/birth/generation gates or retarget a changed candidate.

steps.title: Redo derived from the actual accepted compensation
steps.user: Redo restores Errands. Other eligible causal redo steps remain independently available.
steps.operation: Validate and append the inverse of the actual reviewed action, not the historical Groceries value.
steps.rule: Reviewed compensation affects the selected action; it never silently consumes siblings or substitutes generic recovery.

scenarios.title: Concurrent compensation of the same action
scenarios.summary: Two Macs can each reverse X before learning of the other’s action. Both compensations stay in history. Review depends on the requested Undo/Redo family and current values; reversing one restored note preserves the other.
scenarios.setup: A and B independently prepare Undo of action X. Each commits its own compensation U or V before learning of the other.
scenarios.outcome: Both actions survive. Competing family descendants require scoped review; unrelated later actions retain their own eligibility.

steps.title: Independent admission of Undo X on two Macs
steps.user: Each local capture is checked against its own complete candidate frontier and Current.
steps.operation: Allocate distinct immutable compensation identities and preserve exact undoOf evidence.
steps.rule: There is no distributed exactly-once pop or mutable cross-Mac undo cursor.

steps.title: Candidate derivation after receipt of U and V
steps.user: Equal effects may converge visibly, while competing descendants remain reviewable.
steps.operation: Derive direction-relative candidates and compensation families, keeping every causal action.
steps.rule: After reviewed Redo U, a now-no-op Redo V creates nothing and consumes no eligibility. A separate X family can still undo/redo automatically.

steps.title: Independent fresh-birth mappings for Undo Delete
steps.user: Two concurrent restorations produce distinct fresh births; reversing one preserves the other.
steps.operation: Record exact fresh-birth mapping in each compensation and reverse only the selected mapping.
steps.rule: A later reversal of that deletion needs another fresh birth; no historical branch is collapsed by equal preview bytes.

scenarios.title: Partial native Undo followed by relaunch
scenarios.summary: Partial native Undo saves which effects of a typing action remain. Reopening uses that record and Current’s history to determine portable Undo eligibility, so an already reversed effect is not reversed twice.
scenarios.setup: A saved typing action contains several edits. Native Undo reverses only part, then the app closes and reopens.
scenarios.outcome: The durable remaining-effect claim prevents a later coarse Undo from reversing the already undone part twice.

steps.title: Causal eligibility check before native Undo consumption
steps.user: The existing native text operation runs only after the shared causal router approves its candidate.
steps.operation: Check current text-state/range validity and causal eligibility before consuming a native entry.
steps.rule: A later remote rename can change the eligible action even if native body ranges still look valid.

steps.title: Durable remaining-effect coverage and note compensation
steps.user: The partial reversal records which saved-action effects remain, with exact state references.
steps.operation: Commit the native-coverage compensation together with its complete note effects and dependencies.
steps.rule: Coverage follows action ancestry; incomparable maximal claims require review, not an arbitrary newest claim.

steps.title: Portable candidate reconstruction after reopening
steps.user: Only the remaining eligible effect is proposed. Old Cocoa grouping/selection is not reconstructed.
steps.operation: Build candidates from retained coverage and Current’s represented lineage, including all relevant families.
steps.rule: Saved-edit granularity survives; per-keystroke cross-device stacks and executable native objects do not.

scenarios.title: Shared-note windows during composition and remote publication
scenarios.summary: Two windows share one live note and its Undo owner while keeping independent selections. A remote body update waits for an applicable native input boundary and checks the note, attachment, store, root and lifecycle versions again.
scenarios.setup: Windows X and Y show the same note. X starts composition; Y changes selection or closes while a remote result is pending.
scenarios.outcome: Input uses normal AppKit event delivery. Admitted work survives attachment changes; remote publication waits for an applicable native input boundary and revalidates its captured context.

steps.title: Independent view attachments to one live note
steps.user: Each view has its own selection/scroll while edits belong to the shared note and Undo scope.
steps.operation: Attach observers to one live model; retain remembered cursor updates as private presentation state.
steps.rule: View observers must not duplicate mutation, action registration or pending capture.

steps.title: Native composition while remote publication is prepared
steps.user: Input uses normal native event delivery. A prepared remote body may wait for an applicable native input boundary before publication.
steps.operation: Retain captured attachment/note/generation evidence and defer applicable remote body publication as required by the host bridge.
steps.rule: Composition alone creates no conflict prompt or durable IME buffer. Search remains synchronous.

steps.title: Attachment changes before a late completion
steps.user: Admitted history continues; a late callback cannot target a different attachment or overwrite newer text.
steps.operation: Revalidate the native input boundary, note/root/store/lifecycle generations and attachment identity at the actual consumer.
steps.rule: Closing the last view does not discard pending history. Native keyboard/IME integration still has its own qualification gate.

scenarios.title: Dedicated saved-search windows and bookmark preferences
scenarios.summary: Each saved search reuses its own ordinary window over the shared collection. Activating one preserves the other windows’ searches and selections. Bookmark preferences retain its frame and open state across launches.
scenarios.setup: An ordinary window shows “inbox”. The user activates saved searches Work and Personal, then activates Work again before relaunching.
scenarios.outcome: Each bookmark reuses its dedicated shared-model window. Existing bookmark preferences remember its frame and open state; the collection and note Undo remain shared.
scenarios.contractNote: These contracts cover the shared-editor, synchronous-search and lifecycle seams. Dedicated bookmark activation/frame/reopen acceptance is specified in the linked window feature contract and retains its application integration gate.

steps.title: Bookmark activation and dedicated-window creation
steps.user: A dedicated Work window opens with its saved search and remembered note. The inbox window keeps its own presentation.
steps.operation: The existing bookmark owner routes activation through open-window management and initializes a view over the same live collection.
steps.rule: Search stays synchronous. Query, selection, layout and focus are view state; opening a window creates no second database, writer identity or action branch.

steps.title: Reuse of Work while Personal remains independently presented
steps.user: Personal has its own query. Work’s existing window comes to the foreground instead of duplicating or replacing another view.
steps.operation: Resolve the bookmark-to-window association; edits and per-note Undo continue through the one shared model and causal router.
steps.rule: Commands target the invoking window’s actual note/attachment. Closing a bookmark window releases presentation resources while admitted note work survives.

steps.title: Preference retention and reopening of existing bookmarks
steps.user: Remembered open windows for bookmarks that still exist reopen with their saved searches and placement.
steps.operation: Persist bookmark-scoped frame/open-state through the existing bookmark preference path; rebuild views only after complete current/search readiness.
steps.rule: This is private UI preference data, separate from causal note actions. It does not promise restoration of every arbitrary ordinary window; query-edit/removal behavior remains a named UI decision.

scenarios.title: Durable preservation of a selected unresolved revision
scenarios.summary: Save as new note records the exact copy and disposition for a selected revision while preserving the source history. Independent explicit copies can create different note births. Completed disposition survives later edits or deletion of the copy.
scenarios.setup: Two Macs independently choose Save as new note for exact unresolved revision R of an NV-head conflict.
scenarios.outcome: Each explicit copy may have its own birth. Completed preservation hides only the selected revision’s unresolved attention.

steps.title: Captured preview of source revision R in NV-copy mode
steps.user: The resolver has a captured NV-copy command and exact selected revision.
steps.operation: Validate source revision, selected mode, Current and candidate copy evidence.
steps.rule: A body-equal or already modified/deleted candidate is not automatically exact reusable preservation evidence.

steps.title: Durable copy and source-disposition evidence
steps.user: The new note and completed source disposition become durable before attention is settled.
steps.operation: Commit exact copy/action/provenance evidence and its complete dependency closure.
steps.rule: No source Put/Delete/Keep Current or supersession is emitted just to preserve R.

steps.title: Reconciliation of reciprocal copies and later copy deletion
steps.user: The original plus two recovered copies may remain, even with equal bodies.
steps.operation: Derive unresolved attention from durable completed dispositions while reducing the source independently.
steps.rule: Completed disposition survives copy edits/deletion and reopen; new source descendants remain reviewable.

scenarios.title: Automatic import of an eligible ordinary text file
scenarios.summary: An ordinary unstamped file imports after its origin, availability and narrowly defined repair candidates are checked. One admitted observation keeps the same retry identity. Later discovery of a duplicate preserves independently created notes.
scenarios.setup: An ordinary unstamped txt file appears in the repository. Provenance and availability checks permit inspection, and there is no applicable association or narrowly scoped repair candidate.
scenarios.outcome: NV creates one fresh birth for that admitted observation. If delayed history later reveals a duplicate, both independent births survive.

steps.title: Verified observation and ordinary-file classification
steps.user: NV reads a verified current file through matching complete catalogs around the selected read.
steps.operation: Check availability/provenance and per-note active-path or exact nonempty-content repair exceptions first.
steps.rule: Missing metadata alone does not prompt. Quiet catalogs do not prove that unknown remote history is complete.

steps.title: Admission of one fresh import identity
steps.user: The eligible file becomes a new note through ordinary admission and complete action capture.
steps.operation: Reserve exact observation/operation identity and freeze input values; commit its history and eventual relationship evidence.
steps.rule: Retry of one admitted observation reuses its identity; equal independent files are not globally deduplicated by body/name.

steps.title: Receipt of delayed history after independent import
steps.user: Both independently created births remain; new evidence can change future classification.
steps.operation: Union incoming history and revalidate provenance/associations without rewriting the admitted import’s identity.
steps.rule: Late duplicate knowledge does not retroactively merge unrelated births or replay old consent.

scenarios.title: Projection stamp arriving before its named history
scenarios.summary: A projection stamp can name history that has not arrived yet. NV keeps the file and waits for that exact evidence. Once the represented state and unique association match current bytes, it associates the file without recording a duplicate edit.
scenarios.setup: A note body and bounded projection stamp arrive, but the exact immutable history named by the stamp has not.
scenarios.outcome: NV waits for the named evidence; once exact represented state validates, it associates without an echo Put.

steps.title: Independent observation of body and bounded stamp
steps.user: The file is not imported as a new birth merely because its history is delayed.
steps.operation: Parse bounded advisory metadata and record exact missing locators while preserving body bytes.
steps.rule: Body/xattr arrival is not atomic; a stamp is neither physical authority nor an authenticated substitute for history.

steps.title: Validation of the stamp’s named history and represented state
steps.user: Complete dependencies establish the represented birth/state and exact output digest.
steps.operation: Validate envelope/schema/history and unique association evidence against the actual current file.
steps.rule: Malformed/copied/wrong-collection/stale stamps authorize no alias, overwrite or deletion; uncertainty preserves bytes.

steps.title: Fresh physical association and receipt installation
steps.user: The matching file represents the existing note without manufacturing another note action.
steps.operation: Commit freshly validated relationship/receipt state, then reconcile subsequent external changes normally.
steps.rule: No timeout or quiet-catalog count converts missing named history into a new-birth permission.

scenarios.title: Source change before external-file choice admission
scenarios.summary: A choice previews A, then another editor saves B before approval. NV durably replaces the latest preview after checking its version. The old preparation for A becomes stale and cannot reuse its consent for B.
scenarios.setup: A repair/recovery choice previews external value A. Another editor saves B before the user approves A.
scenarios.outcome: The stale preparation is rejected and the latest durable preview refreshes; prior consent never retargets B.

steps.title: Durable retention and preview of source A
steps.user: The read-only choice shows exact captured A and its proposed target relationship.
steps.operation: Commit the latest verified payload and its reference before reporting durable retention. Keep unadmitted consent process-local.
steps.rule: Merely previewing every external save does not create an archive or an admitted operation.

steps.title: Replacement of the latest verified snapshot with B
steps.user: The latest preview becomes B only after its payload and reference are durable.
steps.operation: Generation-check the snapshot replacement transaction while preserving still-frozen operation references.
steps.rule: Rollback keeps the prior durable pair; an ambiguous outcome is resolved by exact identity lookup.

steps.title: Rejection of the stale A preparation at admission
steps.user: No note mutation occurs from stale consent; the refreshed exact choice needs renewed approval.
steps.operation: Recheck source/target/history/root/claim generations atomically at admission.
steps.rule: A reservation label is not proof that a manual command was admitted, and restart cannot replay consent.

scenarios.title: Source change after external-file operation admission
scenarios.summary: An admitted operation keeps frozen input A while newer B becomes a later observation. After restart, exact saved action evidence determines whether A committed. Receipt recovery continues the same operation and note birth.
scenarios.setup: An operation on external A is admitted. Before history/receipt completion, another editor saves B and the app crashes.
scenarios.outcome: Recovery locates the exact A operation and finishes association/settlement; it does not allocate another birth or discard B.

steps.title: Admission of A with its exact operation link
steps.user: A becomes ordinary pending history with its frozen input and provisional relationship claim.
steps.operation: Atomically revalidate/admit the note mutation and claim after asynchronous preparation/reservation.
steps.rule: Only admission fixes the operation’s exact semantic identity; the receipt is a later physical/accounting result.

steps.title: Retention of latest B alongside unfinished frozen A
steps.user: The recovery graph retains latest B plus frozen A independently.
steps.operation: Durably replace the latest reference without releasing A’s unfinished-operation ownership; complete A’s history barrier.
steps.rule: A later Delete does not erase the earlier import’s committed identity or authorize re-admission into the deleted birth.

steps.title: Recovery of committed A before receipt settlement
steps.user: The same A operation/birth is recovered, even if that birth was later deleted. B remains subsequent work.
steps.operation: Resolve ambiguous SQL outcomes, validate exact operation/action/parent closure, then freshly account for the chosen actual projection and settle links.
steps.rule: Lookup must not ask only whether the birth is currently live. No receipt retry replays the note mutation or old consent.

scenarios.title: Disappearance of an unadmitted pending external file
scenarios.summary: The last durably retained readable file snapshot survives later disappearance or unreadability. Its bytes remain available for a fresh applicable decision or explicit recovery. Association and physical changes still need fresh evidence.
scenarios.setup: A verified external snapshot is pending, then its file disappears or becomes unreadable before a decision.
scenarios.outcome: The last readable snapshot stays privately recoverable; a fresh recovery action needs fresh applicable evidence or explicit choice.

steps.title: Durable latest-snapshot retention
steps.user: The recovery viewer can preview the exact retained bytes.
steps.operation: Commit payload and latest reference together in the private pending graph.
steps.rule: Pending snapshots are not segments, note identity, provider output, or an archive of all unreviewed saves.

steps.title: Current observation of disappearance or unreadability
steps.user: NV preserves the snapshot and reports uncertainty; it does not infer a committed note Delete.
steps.operation: Retain last readable input and reclassify current physical/provenance evidence.
steps.rule: Missing source bytes grant no stale import, restoration, association or physical permission.

steps.title: Fresh preparation of an applicable explicit recovery
steps.user: A separate recovery can create a fresh note from the retained input.
steps.operation: Prepare/approve current target and source evidence, then admit a new exact recovery action through the complete local barrier.
steps.rule: An already admitted operation resumes its own identity; an unadmitted reservation returns to fresh decision work after restart.

scenarios.title: External disappearance during deletion confirmation
scenarios.summary: A missing note file can trigger the configured deletion choice. File return, changed Current or a received Delete can invalidate that choice. A new local Delete needs fresh admission and its complete local save barrier.
scenarios.setup: The external-deletion preference asks about a missing projection. The file may return, the note may change, or remote Delete may arrive.
scenarios.outcome: Revalidate the exact current candidate before a new local Delete; committed received Delete follows its own causal semantics.

steps.title: Preparation of the configured missing-file decision
steps.user: NV retains the live note and prepares the configured external-deletion confirmation.
steps.operation: Capture the exact source relationship, note generation and current absence evidence.
steps.rule: Filesystem disappearance alone is not an immutable Delete and does not erase retained history.

steps.title: Intervening file return, note change or received Delete
steps.user: The old click cannot delete a different generation or remove the returned file.
steps.operation: Invalidate stale source/note/claim evidence and refresh classification before admission.
steps.rule: If remote committed Delete arrives, its separate reducer semantics apply; an association claim cannot suppress it.

steps.title: Fresh Delete admission and exact-snapshot physical effect
steps.user: A newly admitted local Delete takes its complete parent barrier; restoration uses a fresh birth.
steps.operation: Only the original exact-snapshot operation may physically remove a still-matching accepted projection after local durability.
steps.rule: No startup tombstone sweep or physical permission replay follows restart; newer bytes are preserved/reconciled.

scenarios.title: New projection intent C while installation B is unfinished
scenarios.summary: A is the verified note file when update B starts. New intent C arrives before B finishes. B settles only its own output and captured edit versions; C stays pending until its own applicable installation.
scenarios.setup: A is installed. Projection B starts, then a newer intended value C is admitted before B’s result or receipt returns.
scenarios.outcome: B can settle only its captured work. C remains intended/pending until the correct file and receipt evidence exist.

steps.title: Preparation of B against accepted projection A
steps.user: The file plan captures expected A and exact output B.
steps.operation: Bind the projection to the note/root/relationship generations and locally durable represented history.
steps.rule: Mutable note replacement uses the expected-snapshot contract, distinct from immutable object exclusive creation.

steps.title: Admission of newer intent C before B settles
steps.user: The live note and intended projection become C while B retains its own owned inputs.
steps.operation: Record newer pending generations and retain the latest external observation separately from frozen B.
steps.rule: A successful old file write is not evidence that C was installed, and old approval cannot overwrite newer source bytes.

steps.title: Exact-result accounting for B with C still pending
steps.user: The system records only the actual applicable B outcome and still owes C.
steps.operation: Reobserve exact file/claim state, transfer only serviced links into a receipt, and schedule C’s proper projection.
steps.rule: Retiring accepted B for a later observation never clears intended C or manufactures an echo import.

scenarios.title: Scoped disposition of an Apple unresolved version
scenarios.summary: Resolving captured Apple version V requires admission, complete local history durability, exact plaintext installation and final coordinated checks. Only still-applicable captured members are marked resolved, followed by a fresh query.
scenarios.setup: The conflict resolver presents selected Apple unresolved member V. The user chooses Use or Save as new note for that captured member.
scenarios.outcome: Only applicable captured members receive resolved = YES after exact local history, projection and final coordinated checks.

steps.title: Version capture, bounded preview and choice admission
steps.user: Read-only preview is dismissible; per-version waits/errors use bounded attempts.
steps.operation: Capture invocation mode, exact source/member/root observations and selected content; revalidate then admit the chosen action.
steps.rule: Preview/Cancel has no disposition effect. Re-presentation retries applicable work without overlapping accessors.

steps.title: Local-history barrier and exact plaintext installation
steps.user: The action’s complete group/parent barrier and the actual chosen file result must both succeed.
steps.operation: Retain accepted exact history, then install/verify the expected plaintext generation.
steps.rule: Local acceptance alone cannot substitute for the extra file gate; upload is irrelevant.

steps.title: Final coordinated member check and scoped disposition
steps.user: Set resolved only for still-applicable captured members, then verify via a successful fresh query.
steps.operation: Recheck source/member/root/file generations inside the short merging accessor before scoped setters.
steps.rule: No version removal occurs. Failed enumeration is not empty, and empty Apple results cannot clear an NV-head conflict.

scenarios.title: External-editor handoff from an encrypted collection
scenarios.summary: An explicit handoff creates owned plaintext scratch outside the provider folder and discloses external-app retention risks. Returned edits use the ordinary local save barrier. Cleanup applies only to the exact serviced scratch generation.
scenarios.setup: The user explicitly opens an encrypted note in an external editor through a disclosed plaintext scratch file outside the provider folder.
scenarios.outcome: Returned edits are admitted/captured normally; scratch survives until the exact accepted generation is locally durable.

steps.title: Explicit plaintext handoff and scratch creation
steps.user: The explicit action discloses that the other app’s autosave/backup may retain plaintext.
steps.operation: Capture exact note/root/generation and create owned scratch outside the encrypted provider namespace.
steps.rule: Encryption does not implicitly create plaintext projections or authorize undisclosed temporary exports.

steps.title: Read, admission and capture of returned edits
steps.user: NV preserves the returned value as ordinary pending history and freezes the exact handoff generation.
steps.operation: Revalidate read/attachment/current inputs and force asynchronous capture for external settlement.
steps.rule: A failed local barrier retains admitted text and owned scratch. Handoff completion requires that exact generation’s complete local durability barrier.

steps.title: Scratch settlement after exact-generation durability
steps.user: After its complete local barrier, matching owned scratch can settle; newer scratch/work remains.
steps.operation: Check exact-generation completion and the still-identifiable owned resource before cleanup.
steps.rule: Quit/switch owns settlement or explicit cancellation; stale callbacks cannot clear newer work.

scenarios.title: Automatic repair of positively absent same-root NV Data
scenarios.summary: If the same owned root has lost NV Data, a complete private copy can reconstruct it automatically when no unread newer evidence is disclosed. Exclusive creation preserves a competing directory or file that appears meanwhile.
scenarios.setup: The positively owned root remains the same directory. NV Data is positively absent, local closure is complete, and no unread newer evidence is disclosed.
scenarios.outcome: NV transparently reconstructs the known repository; it does not ask Restore or Work Offline for this case.

steps.title: Classification of same-root top-level absence
steps.user: Healthy local editing continues while automatic repository repair starts.
steps.operation: Verify held root identity, exact top-level absence, complete local closure and writable namespace.
steps.rule: Unreadable, offline, foreign or identity-ambiguous is not positive absence; disclosed unread newer evidence uses its own policy.

steps.title: Exclusive reconstruction of the known protocol namespace
steps.user: The complete known descriptors/objects are copied by exact identity.
steps.operation: Exclusively create ordinary protocol directories, verify final names and perform required barriers.
steps.rule: A race winner is reclassified/preserved. Occupied damaged entries remain in place; affected provider writes stop and Save As uses a fresh destination.

steps.title: Verification and resumption of provider publication
steps.user: Sync resumes from the same local history; available remote branches still union later.
steps.operation: Verify the reconstructed known repository and retain all accepted history plus restartable unfinished work.
steps.rule: Foreign collisions stop affected provider effects; cleanup removes only exact owned disposable artifacts.

scenarios.title: Fresh-store repair from complementary retained copies
scenarios.summary: The surviving retained-history pin requires G+L+R. Private history supplies G+L and the repository supplies G+R. Their validated union builds a separate replacement; complete history and the pin must be durable before activation.
scenarios.setup: The surviving pin names closure G+L+R. The damaged private store has G+L; the repository has G+R. Neither alone is complete.
scenarios.outcome: Use the validated union to build a fresh sibling; activate it only after its complete closure and retained pin are durable.

steps.title: Capture and preservation of independently valid repair evidence
steps.user: Recovery preserves the damaged source and identifies independently valid objects from each copy.
steps.operation: Classify identity, entry kind, access, exact authenticated bytes and required closure, not presumed cause or timestamps.
steps.rule: Missing entries never subtract from the repair union; contradictory bytes are not merged into a synthetic payload.

steps.title: Construction of fresh sibling with closure G+L+R
steps.user: The candidate remains unattached while copy/validation/pin work can be interrupted.
steps.operation: Commit complete accepted closure and required private groups, pending links and usable unlock descriptors into a fresh candidate.
steps.rule: A second failure preserves old evidence and leaves the candidate unactivated; provider repair cannot precede private closure.

steps.title: Activation after candidate verification and pin durability
steps.user: The repaired collection reopens through normal startup gates with a fresh session/origin/epoch.
steps.operation: Durably commit the candidate pin, verify activation and selection cutover, then establish new ownership.
steps.rule: Copied state never restores old physical permission or allocation epochs. Preserve displaced evidence.

scenarios.title: Required retained object missing from all available sources
scenarios.summary: A surviving pin names required history missing from the private store, repository and selected backup. Readable current-note rows cannot waive that obligation. Editable publication needs complete repair or an explicit recovery outcome.
scenarios.setup: Current rows exist, but the required retained pin names a missing leaf or descriptor absent from private store, repository and selected backup.
scenarios.outcome: Editable success waits for complete repair or an explicit recovery outcome; an unrelated malformed extra remains a separate case.

steps.title: Detection of a missing required dependency
steps.user: NV reports the exact recovery problem instead of trusting apparently plausible current rows.
steps.operation: Check the required retained closure and distinguish it from unrelated unaccepted/invalid extras.
steps.rule: Derived current rows, timestamps and a valid snapshot tag cannot waive known retained dependencies.

steps.title: Inspection of available exact repair sources
steps.user: Available evidence is preserved while repository/backup reads are bounded.
steps.operation: Try exact named copies and validate complete closure; record unfinished verification/damage durably when possible.
steps.rule: Provider unavailability is not deletion; contradictory/unsupported required data cannot become silent omission.

steps.title: Explicit unresolved-damage or separate salvage outcome
steps.user: The affected collection stays noneditable until its requirements are satisfied.
steps.operation: Offer applicable Retry/another source or explicitly labeled fresh current-note/file salvage with disclosed limits.
steps.rule: Total private-state loss is a distinct classification; it does not invent knowledge of unpublished history that no surviving pin discloses.

scenarios.title: Fresh private-store bootstrap from a selected repository
scenarios.summary: A new Mac, or total loss of private state, needs explicit folder association and complete verified collection-bootstrap history. A verified snapshot can support read-only preview while editing waits for required history and a durable new local pin.
scenarios.setup: The repository is selected explicitly. No old private store survives; initial-import closure may arrive in pieces.
scenarios.outcome: Complete authenticated snapshot preview can be read-only. Editing needs complete bootstrap/closure and a fresh private pin/origin/epoch.

steps.title: Explicit root selection, ownership and profile unlock
steps.user: The selected folder and key are independently validated; no auto-attachment follows a collection-ID match.
steps.operation: Acquire ownership and read bounded descriptors/bootstrap evidence into a fresh private candidate.
steps.rule: An incomplete import is not a successful empty/partial collection. Missing keys keep it locked.

steps.title: Verification of complete initial-import and snapshot evidence
steps.user: A fully authenticated complete snapshot can be previewed read-only while named batches/parents arrive.
steps.operation: Verify genesis commitment, ImportComplete, snapshot pages/counts/digests and required exact history closure.
steps.rule: Usable assembly pages are not accepted causal history. No preview grants editability or globally latest knowledge.

steps.title: Fresh private acceptance and checked editable publication
steps.user: All current/search values and authoring frontiers appear together; portable Undo is reconstructed from action history.
steps.operation: Commit complete acceptance/pin and derived rows, establish fresh origin/writer epoch, and final-check the opening handoff.
steps.rule: Old native stacks, physical permissions and source private settings are not transplanted from repository identities.

scenarios.title: Private backup containing unpublished and pending work
scenarios.summary: A consistent SQLite backup or stopped-writer copy of the complete database and required journals includes unpublished history, private records and pending file inputs. Usable unlocking descriptors accompany encrypted backups. Restore establishes fresh ownership.
scenarios.setup: The provider is offline. The private store holds unpublished accepted actions, settings and pending external-file recovery buffers.
scenarios.outcome: A consistent keyed database backup or quiesced complete pager copy, plus unlock descriptors, preserves the private recovery state.

steps.title: Consistent capture of the complete private backup boundary
steps.user: The backup covers accepted unpublished history, required state and latest/frozen pending links.
steps.operation: Choose a consistent SQLite backup or quiesced complete DB/journal capture under keyed ownership.
steps.rule: A live database-file-only copy is not the specified consistent backup; current rows alone omit history and required state.

steps.title: Inclusion and verification of usable unlock descriptors
steps.user: Encrypted backup recovery has an authorized password/recovery route; password-free recovery needs no Mac secret.
steps.operation: Include the bounded private unlock descriptors alongside the database and verify the captured backup.
steps.rule: A remembered device-bound Keychain item is not promised portable. Encrypted ciphertext alone does not promise unlockability.

steps.title: Restore under freshly validated ownership and session identity
steps.user: Exact retained actions and pending work recover before editing, using fresh session/epoch allocation.
steps.operation: Revalidate root/key/bootstrap/association and complete closure; recover exact admitted external operations before rescanning.
steps.rule: Old receipts require fresh physical evidence and grant no surviving file-delete permission.

scenarios.title: Password unlock with an unavailable remembered key
scenarios.summary: If Keychain is unavailable, a usable wrapped-key descriptor and authorized password can recover the same collection key. Remembering it requires add-only Keychain creation and verified readback before the association references the new item.
scenarios.setup: An encrypted collection’s device-bound remembered key is unavailable or locked, but a usable wrapped descriptor and password survive.
scenarios.outcome: The authorized password unlocks the same collection key; failed unlock preserves ciphertext and never produces empty plaintext.

steps.title: Profile and unlock-route validation before editable opening
steps.user: Notes remain private and noneditable until an authorized key succeeds.
steps.operation: Read bounded provider/private unlock descriptors and distinguish unavailable Keychain from corrupt history.
steps.rule: Profile, key scope and physical association are independently checked; a matching collection ID proves none of them.

steps.title: Password unwrapping and authenticated object decoding
steps.user: The reviewed KDF/descriptor route unwraps CK, then domain-separated keys open database and objects.
steps.operation: Authenticate envelopes before decompression/value decoding; enforce bounds and semantic consistency separately.
steps.rule: Unsupported profiles, malformed input or authentication failure yield typed failure; there is no weaker/plaintext fallback.

steps.title: Optional remembered-key provisioning and association cutover
steps.user: Password unlocking still works if remembering fails.
steps.operation: Provision add-only, read back/validate the signed-app Keychain item, then durably reference it in private association.
steps.rule: No association may point to an unverified key item; ambiguous cutover preserves potentially referenced credentials.

scenarios.title: Same-key password rewrap and full key/profile conversion
scenarios.summary: Changing a password adds another wrapping of the existing collection key while retaining history and old descriptors. A full key/profile change uses a separate destination, verifies output and credentials, and preserves the source until cutover.
scenarios.setup: The collection is unlocked with CK. The requested operation is either a new password wrapping that same CK or a full conversion to a fresh key/profile destination.
scenarios.outcome: Rewrap preserves exact history and old descriptors. A full key/profile change uses a source-preserving fresh destination and verified cutover.

steps.title: Preparation of a same-CK wrapped descriptor
steps.user: The operation explains that old descriptors/secrets may still unlock retained copies.
steps.operation: Prepare a new bounded wrapped-key descriptor for the same CK without changing note/action identities or database key derivation.
steps.rule: Rewrap is not revocation, database rekeying or erasure of provider/APFS copies.

steps.title: Add-only descriptor and credential installation
steps.user: The new unlock route is verified before association refers to it.
steps.operation: Retain/publish exact descriptor bytes and read back independent credential items before private cutover.
steps.rule: Keychain and filesystem are not one transaction; interruption preserves possibly referenced credentials and source data.

steps.title: Fresh-destination path for full key/profile change
steps.user: Current-state conversion is explicitly labeled and verified before switching.
steps.operation: Capture coherent source values, create fresh collection/key/bootstrap, verify complete output and only then change active association.
steps.rule: Source changes invalidate capture. Independent destinations never update/delete source credentials automatically.

scenarios.title: Encrypted history, plaintext output and conversion limits
scenarios.summary: The encrypted profile protects current, historical and deleted values and governs previews and diagnostics. Explicit plaintext output has a disclosed scope and destination. Unsupported rich-text or attachment conversion preserves the source.
scenarios.setup: An encrypted collection contains sensitive current, deleted and historical values. The requested operation is an explicit plaintext export or a conversion whose target may not support the source content.
scenarios.outcome: Encrypted provider/private history stays within its profile; explicit output discloses scope and preserves source on unsupported or failed conversion.

steps.title: Authenticated reading and profile-specific plaintext handling
steps.user: Previews are available in memory; encrypted at-rest values and diagnostics retain their prescribed privacy.
steps.operation: Use bounded authenticated envelopes before decoding; encrypt sensitive private rows/indexes and keep provider IDs opaque.
steps.rule: Authentication does not prove freshness/physical authority. Production diagnostics use closed IDs/counts/status, not titles, paths or keys.

steps.title: Lock or explicitly requested plaintext output
steps.user: Lock releases view-held plaintext. Export/handoff requires an explicit disclosed destination.
steps.operation: Retain ownership of intentional scratch/export output and keep it outside encrypted provider history.
steps.rule: The design does not promise whole-process zeroization or erasure of another app’s backup; those are not inferred from marker tests.

steps.title: Unsupported rich/attachment conversion before cutover
steps.user: The conversion rejects/discloses unsupported loss and preserves source bytes before any cutover.
steps.operation: Choose a supported target codec/profile and detached verified conversion; maintain genuine legacy recovery/export separately.
steps.rule: Attachments are unsupported; RTF/HTML identity/rendering is deferred. Never silently flatten or fetch resources to satisfy a conversion.

scenarios.title: Repository copy with unavailable entries and no private store
scenarios.summary: Copy captures available immutable history, descriptors and associated unknown files. It reports unreadable placeholders or inputs that changed. The source Mac’s Application Support data is outside this repository-copy boundary.
scenarios.setup: A repository is copied from Finder or backup without source Application Support. One provider placeholder is unreadable and an unknown text file is present.
scenarios.outcome: Preserve the exact available captured inventory and report holes/changed inputs. A current-state export remains a separate command.

steps.title: Rooted capture of the repository inventory
steps.user: The requested copy includes visible NV Data, historical objects/descriptors and associated unknown/unimported files.
steps.operation: Use rooted bounded enumeration and capture actual available bytes and known missing/unreadable dependencies.
steps.rule: Source Application Support, unpublished work and other Macs are outside this copy’s scope and are not prerequisites.

steps.title: Verified copying of available exact evidence
steps.user: The destination preserves immutable identities/bytes and reports the unreadable placeholder or changed captured file.
steps.operation: Verify copied inventory; preserve useful available evidence even if editable recovery waits for a missing dependency.
steps.rule: Do not fabricate a new genesis/current-state history or claim global freshness/completeness.

steps.title: Optional explicit switch after destination verification
steps.user: Copy-only leaves the active root unchanged; switching establishes fresh private ownership and epoch.
steps.operation: Explicitly validate destination physical root/bootstrap/key and activate a fresh private association.
steps.rule: Historical lineage and portable Undo transfer through bytes; old root authority, receipts and distributed writer identity do not.

scenarios.title: Current-note recovery after local acceptance failure
scenarios.summary: An admitted edit stays visible when its local save barrier fails. Retry keeps the exact pending identity. Recovery export must include consistent live pending values and verify a fresh destination before releasing source work.
scenarios.setup: An admitted edit is visible but its local SQL barrier fails. The user requests recovery Save As while that live work remains pending.
scenarios.outcome: Retain the live work, retry the urgent barrier or create a disclosed verified current-notes recovery export before transition.

steps.title: Local barrier failure after edit admission
steps.user: The visible pending text remains available; subsequent mutation is gated by local failure policy.
steps.operation: Keep exact capture/retry input and pending generations while classifying committed, failed or uncertain outcomes.
steps.rule: An admitted value is not discarded because I/O failed; ambiguous identity is queried before allocating replacement work.

steps.title: Selection of urgent retry or current-note recovery export
steps.user: The UI distinguishes urgent local retry from a current-notes recovery export that includes live pending values.
steps.operation: Capture a coherent complete source and verify a fresh destination with explicitly disclosed history limits.
steps.rule: A repository-only copy may omit admitted RAM edits and cannot serve as evidence those edits were saved.

steps.title: Verification before source release or collection transition
steps.user: Source live work stays retained until the chosen recovery result is verified and the transition is applicable.
steps.operation: Recheck source generation, required outputs, credentials and physical destination before association cutover.
steps.rule: Failure/cancellation leaves pending work and source intact; an old completion cannot certify newer edits.

scenarios.title: Close with local work pending and provider work stalled
scenarios.summary: One close owner stops new edits and saves complete admitted actions and required private state. After local durability, Quit Without Waiting preserves unpublished history and restartable note-file intent. Failure of rebuildable current rows alone does not block close.
scenarios.setup: Edits and an external-editor handoff are pending. Provider work is stalled and current materialization may fail independently.
scenarios.outcome: One close owner drains mandatory local state. After that, Quit Without Waiting retains unpublished objects and reconcilable file intent.

steps.title: Quiescing and mandatory local close barriers
steps.user: New admission quiesces while existing edits and external handoffs settle or are explicitly canceled.
